He played college basketball for [[West Virginia University]], where he was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. ==High school career== Jones attended [[Mount Vernon High School (New York)|Mount Vernon High School]] in [[Mount Vernon, New York]]. As a junior, he averaged 21 points, 12 rebounds, two blocks per game. As a senior, he averaged 23 points, 14 rebounds, and two blocks per game. In 2006 and 2007, he led Mount Vernon to the New York State PHSAA championships.{{cite web | url=http://www.wvusports.com/profile.cfm?id=101740 | title=5 Kevin Jones | work=wvusports.com | accessdate=July 8, 2014}} ==College career== In his freshman season at [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]], Jones posted eight games in double figures, including a stretch of six games in a row during Big East play. In 35 games, he averaged 6.3 points and 4.9 rebounds in 19.3 minutes per game.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kevin-jones-5.html | title=Kevin Jones Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | accessdate=July 8, 2014}} In his sophomore season, he set a school record with 135 offensive rebounds in a season and was second on the team in three-point field goals made with 42. He was also named to the Big East All-Tournament team and the 76 Classic All-Tournament team. In 38 games (all starts), he averaged 13.5 points, 7.2 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 33.0 minutes per game. In his junior season, he earned All-Big East Honorable Mention honors. In 33 games (all starts), he averaged 13.1 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 34.9 minutes per game. In his senior season, he was named to the All-Big East first team and the NABC Division I All-District 5 first team. In 33 games (all starts), he averaged 19.9 points, 10.9 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.0 blocks in 38.3 minutes per game. ==Professional career== ===2012–13 season=== Jones went undrafted in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. On September 10, 2012, Jones signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/95147/cavs-sign-kevin-jones.html Cavs sign Kevin Jones] However, he was later waived by Cavaliers on October 27, 2012.{{cite web | title=Cavaliers Waive Eric, Jones and Brown | website=NBA | date=2012-10-27 | url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/roster-moves-121027 | access-date=2025-05-11}} On November 1, 2012, he was acquired by the [[Canton Charge]] as an affiliate player. On November 29, 2012, after playing three games for the Charge averaging 27.0 points and 13.7 rebounds per game, Jones re-signed with the Cavaliers. On the same day, he was assigned back to the Charge.{{cite web |title=Canton's Kevin Jones Signs with Cleveland Cavaliers For Third Call-Up of 2012-13 NBA D-League Season |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/cantons_kevin_jones_signs_with_cleveland_cavaliers_2012_11_29.html |work=NBA.com |date=November 29, 2012 |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130513183514/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/cantons_kevin_jones_signs_with_cleveland_cavaliers_2012_11_29.html |archivedate=May 13, 2013 }} On December 4, 2012, he was recalled by the Cavaliers,[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-jones-121204 Cavaliers Recall Kevin Jones] but was sent back to the Charge for other assignments throughout the season.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html 2012-13 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |date=March 27, 2014 }} On December 7, 2012, he debuted for the Cavaliers in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and in eight and a half minutes had 2 points and 4 rebounds.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121207/CLEMIN/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |title=Timberwolves 91, Cavaliers 73 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330123018/http://www.nba.com/games/20121207/CLEMIN/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |archive-date=March 30, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On January 5, 2013, Jones played his best game up to then in the NBA against the [[Houston Rockets]] scoring 6 points and collecting 3 rebounds.[http://www.nba.com/games/20130105/HOUCLE/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore Rockets 112, Cavaliers 104] After that match, coach of Cavaliers [[Byron Scott (basketball)|Byron Scott]] gave more chances to Jones. On April 14, 2013, Jones has played his best game in his first NBA season scoring a double-double, with 11 points and 10 rebounds against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130414/CLEPHI/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |title=76ers 91, Cavaliers 77 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011002809/http://www.nba.com/games/20130414/CLEPHI/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |archive-date=October 11, 2016 |url-status=dead }} ===2013–14 season=== On July 9, 2013, Jones joined the Cleveland Cavaliers for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/summer-league-roster-130709 Cavaliers Announce 2013 Summer League Roster] On July 19, 2013, he was waived by the Cavaliers after not appearing in a summer league game.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/quinn-jones-release-130719 Cavaliers Waive Jones, Quinn] In November 2013, Jones was re-acquired by the Canton Charge.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/canton_charge_announce_201314_2013_11_06.html Canton Charge 2013-14 Training Camp Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203081253/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/canton_charge_announce_201314_2013_11_06.html |date=February 3, 2014 }} On February 3, 2014, he was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=February 7, 2014 }} On March 8, 2014, Jones's contract was bought out by the Charge in order for him to sign with [[San Miguel Beermen]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]].[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4748830 Charge's Kevin Jones Heads to Philippines][http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2014/03/canton_charge_acquire_william.html Canton Charge acquire William Buford, grant Kevin Jones release] ===2014–15 season=== In July 2014, Jones joined the Indiana Pacers for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Rookie/Free Agent Camp Update|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/rookie/free-agent-camp-update|accessdate=July 8, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2014}} On September 26, 2014, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-add-three-players-training-camp-roster Pelicans Add Three Players to Training Camp Roster] However, he was later waived by the Pelicans on October 24, 2014.[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-request-waivers-jones-and-stephens Pelicans Request Waivers on Jones and Stephens] On February 18, 2015, Jones signed with [[Cholet Basket]] of France for the rest of the [[2014–15 LNB Pro A season]].{{cite news|title=Cholet lands Kevin Jones|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/152639/cholet-lands-kevin-jones.html|accessdate=February 18, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=February 18, 2015}} ===2015–16 season=== In July 2015, Jones joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Bucks Announce 2015 Summer League Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-announce-2015-summer-league-roster|accessdate=October 21, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2015}} On October 20, 2015, Jones signed a one-year contract with the Serbian team [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Džons potpisao za Partizan|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=10&dd=20&nav_id=1053721|accessdate=October 20, 2015|work=b92.net|date=October 20, 2015|language=Serbian}} ===2016–17 season=== On August 1, 2016, Jones signed with [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban]] of Russia. He signed a one-plus-one year contract.{{cite news|title=Lokomotiv lands forward Jones|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/766nnnglfruop483/lokomotiv-lands-forward-jones|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821161610/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/766nnnglfruop483/lokomotiv-lands-forward-jones|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 21, 2016|accessdate=August 1, 2016|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=August 1, 2016}} On March 2, 2017, Jones's D-League rights would be traded to the [[Northern Arizona Suns]] in a three-way deal. ===2017–18 season=== On November 27, 2017, Jones signed a two-month contract with Spanish club [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] with an option to extend it for the remainder of the season.{{cite news|title=Baskonia bulks up with Jones|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8cylw5ugbekllijv|accessdate=November 27, 2017|work=EuroLeague.net|date=November 27, 2017}} Following the expiration of his contract, on January 29, 2018, he parted ways with Baskonia.{{cite news|title=Kevin Jones, Baskonia officially parted ways|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/spain/acb/262939/kevin-jones-baskonia-officially-parted-ways.html|accessdate=January 29, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=January 29, 2018}} He continued his season with [[Nanterre 92]] of the French [[LNB Pro A|Jeep Élite]]. Jones was named the Most Valuable Player of the month May.{{Cite web|url=http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Accueil/100004/Article/38222/Kevin-Jones-Joueur-du-mois-de-Mai|title = Accueil}} ===Japan (2018–present)=== In 2018, Jones signed with the [[Ryukyu Golden Kings]] of the [[B.League]]. He then signed with [[Alvark Tokyo]] for two seasons before joining the [[Sun Rockers Shibuya]] in 2021.{{Cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/13b4751625df800a042fc84d6734b138119550be
